package_info.package_versions: Outdated Magento CMS installations (exact versions not specified)
package_info.why_malicious: The ATMZOW Magecart script is malicious because it is injected into e-commerce sites running outdated Magento CMS, with the explicit purpose of stealing sensitive payment and donor information by intercepting and exfiltrating form data entered by users. This enables attackers to harvest credit card and personal data directly from customers without their knowledge or consent.

execution_context.trigger: When a user submits a payment or donation form (runtime event listener on form submission)
execution_context.file_location: Injected JavaScript within payment/donation page templates or static blocks in Magento CMS

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a user submits a payment or donation form, the code attaches an event listener to intercept the form submission, collects all entered form data, and exfiltrates it via an HTTP POST request to a hardcoded attacker-controlled domain, resulting in theft of sensitive user information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script intercepts sensitive form data and sends it to an external, attacker-controlled domain without user knowledge or consent. This is a hallmark of Magecart-style skimming attacks and is not consistent with legitimate e-commerce operations.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate e-commerce JavaScript should only transmit payment or donor data to trusted payment processors or within the site's own infrastructure, never to unknown third-party domains. There should be transparency and user consent for any data transfer.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or payment integrations may send data to trusted third-party services (such as Stripe or PayPal), but only to well-known, reputable endpoints and typically with user consent and visible branding.
key_indicators: JavaScript intercepts form submissions on payment/donation pages
Exfiltration of complete form data to an external, non-legitimate domain
Injected or unauthorized script present in Magento CMS templates or static blocks
No user notification or consent for data transfer outside the site

attack_chain.action: Attacker exploits vulnerabilities in outdated Magento CMS installations to gain administrative access and inject the ATMZOW Magecart JavaScript into payment or donation page templates or static blocks.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious JavaScript is embedded in the site's payment workflow, primed to execute when users interact with forms.

attack_chain.action: When a user submits a payment or donation form, the injected JavaScript intercepts the form submission event and captures all entered data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive payment or donor information is harvested by the malicious script.

attack_chain.action: The script transmits the captured form data to a remote attacker-controlled server via an HTTP POST request.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen payment and donor information, enabling further abuse or sale of the data.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code on payment or donation pages that intercepts form submissions and sends data to external domains not associated with the site or known payment processors
Unexpected or unauthorized network requests initiated from client-side code during form submission events
Presence of obfuscated or unauthorized scripts injected into Magento CMS templates or static blocks, especially those referencing external domains
file_indicators: Injected JavaScript code within Magento CMS template files or static blocks related to payment/donation workflows
References to external domains in script tags or inline JavaScript that are not associated with legitimate payment processors (e.g., Stripe, PayPal, Authorize.net)
network_indicators: HTTP or HTTPS POST requests from client browsers to domains not associated with the e-commerce site or recognized payment providers
Outbound connections to suspicious, newly registered, or previously unseen domains from payment or donation pages
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor e-commerce and donation pages for unauthorized JavaScript that intercepts form submissions and transmits data to unknown external domains. Deploy web application firewalls (WAF) to detect and block suspicious outbound requests from client browsers. Regularly audit Magento CMS templates and static blocks for injected or obfuscated scripts, and monitor for unauthorized changes to files associated with payment workflows. Correlate network traffic with known legitimate payment processor domains to identify anomalous destinations.
